Five Apple Watch models can measure your blood pressure, potentially alerting you to possible high blood pressure. However, they do not provide actual blood pressure readings.

A few smart rings and other fitness devices can do this, but they need regular calibration with a traditional upper-arm blood pressure monitor. The upcoming Signal Ring claims to provide full blood pressure measurements without any calibration, and says that trials involving thousands of people support this claim……

"Silent Killer"

Abnormally high blood pressure (hypertension) and abnormally low blood pressure (hypotension) can both pose significant health risks.

Of the two, high blood pressure is the more dangerous, often referred to as the "silent killer," because it can cause serious and irreversible damage to the arteries, heart, and brain without any obvious symptoms. In many cases, it is only discovered after triggering a heart attack or stroke.

Older adults in particular should monitor their blood pressure regularly, and home upper-arm blood pressure monitors are widely available for self-measurement. However, it would of course be ideal if the fitness device you are already wearing could monitor it fully automatically.

Apple Watch Blood Pressure Feature

The launch of watchOS 26 enables five Apple Watch models to measure blood pressure:

  • Apple Watch Series 11
  • Apple Watch Series 10
  • Apple Watch Series 9
  • Apple Watch Ultra 3
  • Apple Watch Ultra 2

However, these devices will not give you any readings, but only alert you when potential signs of high blood pressure are detected. Other devices such as the Oura Ring operate in a similar way.

Some fitness devices can indeed provide actual blood pressure readings, but they need regular calibration using readings from a blood pressure monitor.

Signal Ring

Startup company Vital Signals says it has developed a smart ring that can measure blood pressure as accurately as a traditional upper-arm blood pressure monitor without any calibration: the Signal Ring.

According to Bloomberg, CEO Tom Moss said he almost died from undiagnosed high blood pressure, which is why he founded the company.

The ring will go on presale later today, ship in October, priced at US$399, with no subscription required. The companion app (see image above) displays real-time blood pressure readings as well as long-term blood pressure trends.

It is worth noting that the Oura Ring has not yet been approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA), but clinical trials have shown that it can provide accurate blood pressure readings for thousands of participants.

Interestingly, Moss does not intend to sell this ring to everyone. He says these professional features are best suited to older adults and people who have been assessed by a doctor as being at risk of high blood pressure, implicitly suggesting that the Signal Ring is relatively average in other areas (such as sleep tracking).
